subject: Partial throughput regression impacting production recommendations - commercial & remediation discussion

Cc: procurement@cloudworks.com, CloudWorks SRE <sre@cloudworks.com>
Date: 2027-01-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Throughput regression affecting live recommendations
message_1_body:
Hi Mateo,

We observed a significant drop in throughput and spike in 5xx/latency across our recommendations traffic starting ~08:50 PST this morning. Impact: our real-time recommendations rate fell ~45% and p99 latency jumped from ~120ms to over 1.2s. This is affecting time-sensitive features for several high-value customers.

Attached are the service logs and a screenshot of the alert thresholds (svc-errlogs-20270109.tar.gz, screenshot-thresholds.png). Our SRE is seeing repeated model inference timeouts and rejected requests. We need an immediate mitigation and a clear remediation path.

We also need confirmation on commercial remediation — given the customer impact we expect SLA credits and a contracting path to ensure this does not recur. Please escalate to execs as needed; I can pull in Procurement depending on the remedy.

Thanks,
Alice Turner
Head of Product Operations
CloudWorks

--
Alice Turner
CloudWorks

- Acknowledged the regression at ~08:50 PST.
- We’re seeing autoscaler backlog + a KV cache thrash pattern that explains repeated cold-starts and higher latency.
- Immediate mitigation being applied: temporarily increase reserved slots for your tenant and engage a soft throttle on non-critical background scoring to relieve head-of-line blocking.

Can we do an executive sync at 10:30 PST? I want to have a clear technical remediation proposal and a commercial proposal for credits before that call.

We’ll follow up with a remediation ETA and a proposed credit calculation.

— Mateo

Subject: Re: Throughput regression affecting live recommendations — triage notes
message_3_body:
Mateo / team — quick technical status for the incident channel: 

Observations:
- During the spike, a recent autoscaler heuristic incorrectly reduced pre-warmed model slots during a high-burst window. The consequence: repeated cold initializations and KV cache misses for long-context requests.
- Error signature in logs: repeated inference_timeouts around 3000ms followed by gateway 502s when queue depth exceeded the per-tenant soft-limit.

Immediate fixes applied (in progress):
1) Force override to reserved-capacity +20% for CloudWorks for the next 3 hours (hot-path).
2) Revert autoscaler commit 7f9a2 for affected pool; will land a rollback within 30–45 minutes.
3) Apply a temporary request-shaping rule to deprioritize <non-critical-feed> scoring endpoints.

Estimated service normalization: 45–90 minutes after rollback fully in. Permanent fix plan: a patch to autoscaler heuristics + KV cache warm-up logic; target delivery: 3 weeks with a staged canary between dev and Dedicated fleets.

Attaching a trimmed error bundle to the thread for reference.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi Alice / Procurement team —

Apologies for the impact. We want to move quickly on a transparent, provisional remedy while we complete root cause and the postmortem. Proposed commercial remediation (provisional):

- Provisional credit equal to 30% of the prorated monthly committed spend for the affected window (08:50–10:00 PST).
- If final postmortem identifies broader rollback window or additional impact, we’ll adjust credits upward; final calculation to be shared in 7 business days.
- As a goodwill gesture: offer 90 days of discounted dedicated pool access (10% discount on Dedicated list pricing) to stabilize workload during the remediation period.

To proceed: please confirm acceptance of the provisional credit offer so Finance can issue a credit note. If Procurement wants a contract amendment to codify a longer-term SLA/priority capacity arrangement, we can loop Legal and propose an addendum.

Attachments: cloudworks-invoice-2027-01.pdf (for reference).

Subject: Remediation plan, timeline, and commercial options
message_6_body:
Hi Alice / CloudWorks execs — following up from the triage call. Summary and concrete next steps: 

Technical remediation and schedule:
- Immediate: rollback autoscaler commit and increase reserved slots (hotfix) — in progress and expected normalization within 60–90 minutes from 09:28.
- Short-term (1–3 days): stabilize canary-level config and extend warm-up windows for heavy-context models.
- Medium-term (3 weeks): full autoscaler heuristic patch + KV cache warm-up logic with staged canary and validation.
- Rollback plan: if the hotfix causes unexpected regressions we will revert within 15 minutes and maintain the temporary reserved slots.

Commercial remediation options proposed:
A) Provisional credit (as proposed) = 30% prorated for affected window, final adj after postmortem.
B) Alternative: fixed SLA-credit table — for sustained p99 > 500ms for >45 minutes, credit = 50% of prorated period; for successive 5xx >2% for >30 minutes, credit = 100% of prorated period (we can draft firm language).
C) Goodwill option: 90-day discounted Dedicated pool (10% off) + priority capacity queuing for CloudWorks during business hours.

Next commercial/legal steps:
- We will prepare a draft addendum with the fixed SLA-credit table (Option B) and the Dedicated pool terms and share a redline within 3 business days.
- If Procurement approves provisional credit quickly, Finance can issue the credit note the same week.

Please confirm which commercial option you prefer and we’ll route Legal to prepare the formal amendment.

— Rishi Malhotra
VP, Customer Reliability & Platform Programs
Redwood Inference
